question: How can a taxonomy or navigation reorganization preserve object/capability identity, scoped findability and explicit unresolved mappings across a larger inventory, without treating a rename, broad/narrow mapping or equal item counts as semantic equivalence?
why_next: R03 fixes the demonstrated P1 mandatory-reachability hole. R02 left large-inventory migration and old-entry identity only partially exercised.
scope_boundary: A owns information inventories, classification decisions, source-to-target meaning and entry mappings. Redirect execution, state and permissions remain B/C; user comprehension and production migration performance remain D.
research_plan: Two independent researchers using verified imozuru CLI; one standards/methods track, one operational counterexample track; then sankai decomposition, parent implementation and independent critic. No new unit if existing units can represent the conditions.
known_sources: All registry/A/sources records; duplicates receive no novelty credit.
